# Sum of a two-limb number and a limb

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/Statements.v, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `add_2_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x + a$:

$$z \approx x + a.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x + a` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | `Expansion<T, 2>` |  |
| `a + x` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` |  |
| `x += a` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | `Expansion<T, 2>` |  |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - (x + a)\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x + a\rvert$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`; `kairn::traits` exports them rounded up to `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $2^{-105} \approx 2.4652 \times 10^{-32}$ | $2^{-47} \approx 7.1054 \times 10^{-15}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1p-47f`, `0.0f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1.0000000000001p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1.000002p-47f`, `0.0f` |

The compiled constants are those of `kairn::traits<Expansion<T, 2>>::add_limb`: `unit` and `tiny` bound the error relative to the exact result, `unit_computed` and `tiny_computed` relative to the computed one ($\lvert \text{error}\rvert \le \mathtt{unit\_computed}\,\lvert\text{computed}\rvert + \mathtt{tiny\_computed}$).

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits and any exponent range, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `add_2_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Add21.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Add21.v), against `add_2_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition add_2_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (3 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 a : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  let '(z0, z1) := add_2_1 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 a in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((x0 + x1) + a)) <= 2 * u prec ^ 2 * Rabs ((x0 + x1) + a).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** [JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 4 (DWPlusFP); bound from [MR22](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#mr22). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/add_2_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/add_2_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`, rounded to nearest; `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum`](two_sum.md), [`fast_two_sum`](fast_two_sum.md).

```
# DWPlusFP: a double-word number plus a number of the format.

(sh, sl) = two_sum(x0, a)
v        = add(x1, sl)
(z0, z1) = fast_two_sum(sh, v)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#add_2_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 64 298 000 | 0 | 0.940060 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 64 285 624 | 0 | 0.992645 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 12 218 888 | 0 | 0.939450 (`fp:5:-6:3`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only `from_limbs_unchecked` or writing `limb[]` directly can make.
